feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector leadership experience. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear executive profile: the header and experience consistently position you as a digital platform, governance, and communications leader.  
- Good credibility signals: scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and concrete platforms/tools strengthen impact.  
- Broad yet coherent scope: strategy, CMS, analytics, multimedia, and AI/search are integrated well for mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space for more quantified outcomes.  
- Add more results language: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance where possible.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler; maintain consistent capitalization and punctuation across bullets. Minor style inconsistencies include “AI-enabled” vs. “AI Hybrid Search,” and date formatting such as “Oct. 2024 – Present” vs. “Sept. 2018.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is broad and repeats several ideas already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with a more direct verb structure: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one high-value proof point from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase credibility.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and multimedia/AI experiences.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivered large-scale platform and analytics improvements, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views, while building editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled content experiences for mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” echoes the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure.
- Emphasize highest-value areas tied to recent roles: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and multimedia operations.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider using this section for sharper differentiators rather than repeating the same categories.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well established elsewhere; keep only if targeting advocacy-focused roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes or scope will make it more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed/Launched X to achieve Y.”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for ongoing expansion”; spell out “10 × 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this rewrite style: “AI Hybrid Search — Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely repeat current freelance/NACo experience; keep the footer more project-focused than responsibility-focused.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “production and distribution” are somewhat generic; replace with distinctive deliverables if possible.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented leadership entry. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact themes and avoid repeating Drupal, governance, analytics, and AI-search details already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Open with outcome + client context: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into fewer, stronger ones: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics with governance/usability/operating practices.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishers enabled, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, or workflow time saved.
- Use sharper verbs and reduce implementation detail: “Built Drupal-based campaign microsites and modular storytelling/toolkit experiences” and “Led AI-enabled search strategy, including retrieval design and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Drupal platform,” “governance,” “analytics,” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in skills/footer; don’t restate all of them at full length here.
- This role overlaps heavily with NACo work; emphasize consulting impact, current scope, and new initiatives rather than repeating prior responsibilities.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team/operating ownership, and measurable business impact.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise platform modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Tighten bullets around outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add impact where possible for channels/studio/analytics: audience growth, production cost savings, faster reporting, improved engagement, reduced vendor reliance, or stronger campaign performance.
- Replace softer phrasing like “strengthened”/“expanded” with action + result: “Implemented governance standards and cross-department planning workflows that improved publishing consistency and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” and recurring video/programming overlap with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise ownership and transformation.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may overlap with footer projects; keep the CV item strategic, not project-detail heavy.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for county officials nationwide.”
- Tighten bullets and use stronger verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable growth if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-team campaigns supported.
- Rephrase for ownership and impact: “Built a cross-functional editorial planning process across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and campaign coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards; keep this version focused on operational execution, not enterprise governance.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/regularizing the channel, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths rather than broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector, policy, and advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy and planning
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” styles inconsistently.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Scalable editorial governance for complex, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/core competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than experience-backed strengths like governance, platform modernization, or cross-department coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a value-focused skills summary. It also overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section, so this version should emphasize higher-level execution and recent strengths rather than repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery (including modernization and modular content architecture)”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API integrations, workflow automation; de-emphasize older/basic items like jQuery
- Tighten and group related items: “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” instead of listing all separately; “Airtable and workflow systems” instead of “Airtable systems”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and content architecture • WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages • HTML, CSS and JavaScript • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let the technical section hold the full tool inventory.
- “CMS modernization” and “Web & CMS administration” already appear elsewhere; avoid repeating both phrases verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for the most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and keep it distinct from the broader “Data analytics & reporting” competency and NACo bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Digital analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Group tools and methods more cleanly: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery.”
- Replace vague items with sharper phrasing: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Consider: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI & BigQuery • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding • SEO, UX and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader “Digital strategy & transformation” / “Data analytics & reporting” language; keep this item focused on analytics and optimization.
- Tool names already appear in the Director of Digital Media entry, so avoid repeating too many platform details elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and slightly dated compared with your stronger recent leadership story. Tighten it to emphasize production capability that clearly supports the studio build and event delivery work in your 2022–2024 role.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for impact and specificity: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera operation • Studio buildout and operations • Hybrid/virtual event production”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast video production” or “Video production, editing, and live switching” if accurate; it sounds more senior and distinctive.
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid overly broad wording like “Livestreaming”; “Livestream and webcast delivery” is sharper.
- If space allows, add one higher-value capability tied to recent work, such as “in-house studio operations” or “advocacy/event programming production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; keep this version more technical/tactical.
- Avoid repeating generic “video” language already covered in multiple NACo roles unless you add specificity.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” For a recent, impact-focused CV, this item should either be tighter or signal level of use, especially around Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise CMS, migrations, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of just names: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress/SharePoint (administration) • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Keep wording consistent with recent roles; Drupal should clearly lead given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Consider dropping “GitHub Pages” if it was minor compared with enterprise CMS work; replace only if another platform is more relevant.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools.
- Avoid repeating platform names in multiple sections unless one version adds level, scope, or recency.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and consistency: **HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)**
- Drop version numbers unless required: **HTML5/CSS3** → **HTML/CSS** for cleaner, more current phrasing.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: **Front-end:** HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery | **Implementation:** API integrations, GTM | **Deployment/automation:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work, e.g. “Used for Drupal front-end implementation, tagging, and deployment workflow support.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with **GitHub Actions** here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” positioning elsewhere. Make it more selective and framed around systems-building, not just collaboration apps.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Prioritize higher-signal tools first and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop lower-value or dated items unless central to target roles: **Basecamp** is the easiest cut.
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: **Workflow automation, project intake, editorial coordination, and cross-team collaboration using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, and Teams.**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same exact phrasing here.
- Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp, Slack, and Teams are partly generic workplace tools; keep only those you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email is a recurring strength in recent NACo roles, frame these as platforms used for large-scale member communications and engagement rather than just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(used to support newsletter, campaign, and member engagement programs)_
- If accurate, add scale/context inline: **…for newsletters reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep platform names concise and standardized; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter scale here if it already appears prominently in NACo experience bullets.
- This should stay platform-focused; broader email strategy/governance is already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a tighter tools/methods list and avoid broad nouns like “Dashboarding.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • SEO analysis**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with specific platforms already listed, or with a clearer capability like **KPI reporting** only if not repeated elsewhere.
- Consider adding **Google Search Console** if SEO is a real hands-on skill; “SEO” alone is broad and less credible than a named tool/capability.
- Order by strongest/recently used tools first: **GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio** aligns with recent NACo experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two.
- **A/B testing** is fine here only if supported by examples elsewhere; otherwise it may feel unsubstantiated.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role clearly foundational: team-building, early platform/content execution, and light people guidance.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience/reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the close: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If metrics are unavailable, use operational outcomes: faster publishing, more consistent cross-channel delivery, expanded in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generically and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities, while contributing to digital storytelling and multimedia communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and use stronger verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Cut vague phrasing like “organizational programs and policy work” and “multimedia materials”; replace with “county policy and program priorities” and “digital storytelling/multimedia communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, or cross-team stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid over-claiming broad digital leadership here; save that emphasis for the more recent NACo roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads more like a mixed skills/category list than a sharp technical tools entry. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and “Video production and editing / Livestreaming / Studio operations” elsewhere, so it should focus on specific software and distinctive production capabilities.

Suggested edit
- Tighten to named tools + specialized production skills only; remove generic phrasing.
